etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French stupide, from Latin stupidus (“struck senseless, amazed”), from stupeō (“be amazed or confounded, be struck senseless”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tup-, *(s)tewp- (“to push, stick”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tew- (“to push, hit”). Cognate with Old High German stubarōn (“to be astonished, be stunned, be blocked”). Related also to Old English stoppian (“to block, stop”). See stop.

definitions.definition: Exhibiting the quality of having been done by someone lacking in intelligence.

quote.citation: 2014 May 1, John Barker, Futures: A Novel‎[1], PM Press, page 131:
quote.text: I should have spoke to him there and then, seen he was in the mood to do something stupid.

definitions.definition: Unpleasant; annoying to the speaker. This sense can be used alongside obscene words.

quote.citation: 1982 December 11, Andrea Loewenstein, “The Joys of Community or Holiday-itis Strikes Back”, in Gay Community News, volume 10, number 21, page 12:
quote.text: Marcie Linguini, who had come down with a stupid ear infection the day of Thanksgiving vacation, curled deeper into her bed.

definitions.definition: (euphemistic, by association)   Usually replaces an obscene or profane word, and thus is audibly stressed as such.

quote.text: Mom: Oh you stupid car!  What's wrong with you now?!?Calvin: That's it, Mom! Go ahead and swear! We don't mind!
Calvin, be quiet and eat the stupid lima beans.

quote.citation: 2018, “The Secret(s) of Castle McDuck!”, in DuckTales:
quote.text: Dewey: "It's too narrow for all three of us. Oh, bummer!"Huey: "Or we could just go single file."Dewey: "Stupid smart Huey..."

definitions.definition: (archaic) Characterized by or in a state of stupor; paralysed.

quote.text: No sigh to rise, no tear had pow'r to flow, Fix'd in a stupid lethargy of woe.

definitions.definition: (archaic) Lacking sensation; inanimate; destitute of consciousness; insensate.

quote.text: Were it not for [fire], the whole wou'd be one great stupid inanimate mass.

definitions.definition: Dulled in feeling or sensation; torpid.

quote.citation: 1815, Jane Austen, Emma, volume III, chapter 7:
quote.text: She had never seen Frank Churchill so silent and stupid. He said nothing worth hearing—looked without seeing—admired without intelligence—listened without knowing what she said.
Richard DeLongpre: Aw, we did, didn't we? I'm sorry. I'm so stupid in love with you.

quote.citation: 2013, Lady Gaga (lyrics and music), “Jewels N' Drugs”, in Artpop:
quote.text: I'm your mother, sister, your father, brother / This family is stupid attractive

quote.citation: 1910, Saki [pseudonym; Hector Hugh Munro], “The Strategist”, in Reginald in Russia and Other Sketches, London: Methuen & Co. […], →OCLC, page 87:
quote.text: "You stupid!" screamed the girls, "we've got to guess the word. Now you'll have to go back and think of another."
"What a stupid I am!" Harry exclaimed, as she watched the man ride away in the distance.

quote.citation: 1972, “Smoke on the Water”, performed by Deep Purple:
quote.text: Some stupid with a flare gun burned the place to the ground.
At least those stupids got their money's worth out of this country before they burnt their lungs out.

definitions.definition: (colloquial, uncountable) The condition or state of being stupid; stupidity, stupidness.
